articles.description: Grid, flexibility, and transmission constraints amid limited battery storage forced India to curtail as much as 118.6 gigawatts (GW) of solar and wind power capacity in September, data by India’s JMK Research & Analytics showed. articles.description: Kinder Morgan has committed $4.7bn as its share of investments in two natural gas pipeline joint ventures (JV), driven by increasing demand from power generation, data centres, and liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facilities.

articles.title: Record Fuel Prices Accelerate Europe’s EV Sales
articles.description: Record-high gasoline and diesel prices across Europe are accelerating a shift toward electric vehicles and hybrids while new registrations of conventional cars continue to plummet by double digits in key markets. Total car sales in Europe, including the UK, Norway, and Switzerland, rose by 10.2% in September from a year earlier, data from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA) showed on Thursday. articles.title: India's Middle East Oil Imports Jumped 32% in September
articles.description: India saw its crude oil imports from the Middle East rebound in September to pre-war levels amid higher volumes exiting the Strait of Hormuz, while competition from China for Russian oil resulted in declining imports from Russia. India’s crude oil imports from the Middle East jumped to 2.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in September, up by 32% compared to August and the highest level since February, according to vessel-tracking data compiled by Reuters. articles.title: Iran Claims Seven Ships Hit in Persian Gulf as Oil Prices Surge
articles.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy on Thursday claimed that seven vessels, including oil tankers, were either hit by Iranian forces or struck mines in the Persian Gulf over the past day, as tensions in the region flared up again this week. The IRGC Navy said that its forces had tracked and hit four tankers carrying out oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf, while three other vessels hit mines west of the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: India Ramps Up Coal Supplies to Record High as Power Crisis Looms
articles.description: Coal supply for power plants in India is ramping up and will soon normalize, an unnamed senior official from the energy ministry in New Delhi said, as quoted by Reuters. At the moment, coal power generators are getting 2.6 million tons of coal daily, which is a record high, the official also said. The news comes on the heels of a warning that as many as 96 coal power plants in the country only had coal stocks for three days of consumption, according to data from India’s Central Electricity Authority. articles.title: Iran’s Oil Reserves Run Dry as U.S. Naval Blockade Tightens
articles.description: Iranian oil in floating storage has been drained amid the U.S. Navy blockade, the Wall Street Journal has reported, citing Kpler data that suggests further tightening in global oil supply. “There’s no more oil to discharge to China anymore,” Kpler’s head of crude oil analysis, Homayoun Falakshahi, said, as quoted by the WSJ. Before the United States imposed a blockade on Iranian ports in April, Iran had close to 150 million barrels in floating storage, the report said. articles.description: The world’s ongoing energy crisis is quickly turning into a global food security crisis. articles.title: As BP Leaves the North Sea, These Independents Are Buying In
articles.description: Back in July, UK oil and gas major BP Plc. (NYSE:BP) announced that it was putting its entire UK North Sea oil and gas business up for sale as part of a broader $20-billion portfolio overhaul, marking the end of a 60-year era as a leading player in Europe's largest oil basin. BP's North Sea operations produced about 117,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025 (roughly 5% of BP's total global output) and employed around 1,100 people. BP is hardly alone.
